takeaways: Generative pages let you keep the out-of-the-box strengths of a model-driven app and extend only the UI where it falls short.
For production-ready generative pages, build them through a coding tool such as VS Code with GitHub Copilot and Microsoft's skill rather than the maker portal, which is best for trying things out.
As AI makes app creation fast, the hard parts become process design, adoption and governance, so makers should invest in designing processes first.
hook: Generative pages promise AI-built UIs in Power Apps, but how do you get from a quick demo to something an enterprise can maintain? Microsoft MVP Sara Lagerquist explains when to extend model-driven apps with generative pages, why the code-first route beats the maker portal, and how governance and process design keep citizen-built apps under control.
